To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the conversational memory of the robot is not used by the participants to create rapport and coordination, (2) the participants do not engage in a coordinated manner with the robot, and (3) the participants are not aware of the conversational memory and do not engage in the recall of previous conversations.
it is hard to maintain social identity and coordination in a long-term human-agent conversation.

1) it is hard to maintain a coherent relationship with a robot over time; 2) it is hard for a robot to maintain a coherent conversational relationship with an individual human; 3) users are more willing to engage in a long-term conversation if the robot signals its memory of previous interactions, and; 4) users contribute to the conversation by asking questions and providing answers, and are more engaged when the robot responds to their input.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the challenges in exploiting conversational memory to maintain social coordination and coherence in human-agent interaction.
how to leverage conversational memory to create a sense of social coordination over time.
how to design agents that can maintain a coherent social identity over time, by revisiting past episodes with users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of conversational memory is challenging, but it is also rewarding, as it allows for a more human-like and engaging interaction.

it is very difficult for an agent to maintain a social relationship over time, and this difficulty is not due to the lack of memory mechanisms but to the difficulty in adapting to the users' contributions.
the results of the study indicate the difficulty to leverage the shared memory with individual users and the need for explicit recall of previous conversations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is challenging to leverage conversational memory in long-term interaction.

the design of conversational memory in long-term human-agent interactions is a challenging endeavor that requires a better understanding of the social coordination mechanisms involved in human-human interactions.
we are able to show that the use of conversational memory is a promising way to create rapport in human-agent interaction, and that the design of the dialog management is crucial for its success.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to maintain a social relationship over time, an agent must be able to remember and revisit past conversations with individual users and also accommodate to expected social coordination patterns.
the way people use language in human-to-human conversations is very different from the way people use it with machines.
, to maintain a long-term relationship, an agent needs to be sensitive to the way that users interact and adapt to their behavior, while also maintaining a consistent and engaging social identity.
